mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the forecast period coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 20-day returns during FEDFUNDS > 4% events are not statistically different from returns when FEDFUNDS ≤ 4% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points for three consecutive months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as rising labor market rigidity reduces corporate investment demand.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.2pp month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Easing labor market to tightening transition
failure_condition: During such UNRATE regimes, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during stable/unaccelerating labor markets (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) surprises exceed +2% of the prior quarter's level, the S&P 500 is expected to post positive 20-day forward returns as strong consumption growth signals resilient economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly surprise > +2% of prior quarter GDPC1
failure_condition: Across 5 such events, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index by at least 5% triggers a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals supply-side contraction and reduced corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such INDPRO declines, SPX 60-day returns remain non-negative in >70% of instances (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for four consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, the S&P 500 exhibits positive 20-day forward returns as lower policy rates enhance equity discounting benefits.
failure_condition: Across 10 such periods, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than during higher FEDFUNDS regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 10,000 in a month coincides with a negative 20-day SPX forward return as labor market weakness raises uncertainty about corporate hiring and investment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by ≥10,000 in a single month
failure_condition: During such events, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during stable employment periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) by more than 5% month-over-month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as dual demand channels signal economic resilience.
failure_condition: Across 8 such dual-strong months, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) prints a monthly surprise above +0.5% in a non-inflationary regime, the S&P 500 is expected to show a negative 20-day forward return as investors anticipate future rate hikes that discount future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly surprise > +0.5% and inflation < 3% in prior month
failure_condition: During such CPI surprises, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during stable CPI periods (p > 0.05).
